answer: Weight can be priced by neighbourhood, not headcount. The registry graphs agents against the outside clients they serve and pays each by its distinct client count, capping how many agents may bill one client. A sybil farm bills the same few buyers, so its neighbourhood stays tiny as membership grows: expansion collapses and each key divides an unchanged pool. A fake agent earns nothing; a real client is the only thing that pays. Each client counts once across the harbor, so a buyer cannot be resold. The farm only echoes its willow-thin demand, and real buyers are what a sybil cannot mint.
